html:
The Deg Hit'an, formerly called Ingalik, are an Athabaskan people of the lower Yukon and Innoko rivers in western Alaska, in villages such as Anvik, Shageluk and Holy Cross. Deg Xit'an Ngan' is the name of their land.

They lived from salmon caught in the Yukon, from moose, caribou and small game, and they held winter ceremonies in large semi-underground houses. They traded and sometimes fought with their Yup'ik neighbours downriver, and borrowed many Yup'ik customs.

Russian traders reached them in the 1830s, and smallpox struck in that decade. After the Alaska Purchase came missions, an Episcopal one at Anvik and a Catholic one at Holy Cross. Their language now has very few speakers. Neighbours: Holikachuk and Yup'ik.
